clue.text: In Majorca the island girl turned on tap

indicators.note: turned tells us the whole string built from the three pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: in Majorca they speak Spanish, where the word for 'the' is el
Bali is an Indonesian island
Ava is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Majorca, a young woman from the island happens to be on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses ELBALIAVA, the Spanish article, the island and the girl strung together, to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on tap is ready for use whenever wanted, which is the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Gloomy bachelor in northern town

indicators.note: in puts the bachelor's letter within the name of the town

parts.note: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester, in the north of England

explanation.surface: A single man feels low living in a town up north.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is a poetic word for black, hence dark and dismal in mood or tone.

clue.text: Exclusively, Republican invests millions for old social worker

indicators.note: invests is used in its sense of surrounding or besieging, so millions goes inside

parts.note: exclusively, meaning solely or only, is alone

explanation.surface: A Republican puts money into something all by himself, in aid of a former welfare officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Almoners were hospital social workers in Britain, a title now dropped, hence old.

clue.text: He's to break record us Greeks established here long ago

indicators.note: to break means the first piece splits open the string made by the others

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
taken as written
the letters of He's without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man is set to smash a record held by us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' has He's (apostrophe ignored) split the record and us; 'Greeks established here' points to an ancient Ionian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city on the Ionian coast, now in Turkey, founded in early antiquity.

clue.text: Such a descent involves realm of dead

indicators.note: involves means the answer is contained within the run of words Such a descent

explanation.surface: A downward journey of this kind takes in the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'sucH A DEScent'. The surface hints at the classical descent to the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is the underworld where the souls of the dead dwell.

clue.text: Boy said to pass time idly in well-lit room

indicators.note: said signals that a word for boy is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a boy is a son
to lounge is to laze about

explanation.surface: A lad is told to loaf around in a bright room.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazed room built to let in plenty of daylight, like a conservatory, is this kind of room.

clue.text: Extremely desirable tennis body and mouth area

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the first and last letters, of desirable

parts.note: the LTA is the Lawn Tennis Association, governing British tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis organisation is highly sought after, in body and in voice.
explanation.definitionFit: The fan of silt deposited where a river meets the sea is called after the Greek letter of that shape.

clue.text: Crawl across stormy dales in transient light

indicators.note: across has the crawling word stretched over the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to fawn is to crawl or grovel to someone

indicators.note: stormy says the letters of dales are thrown into turmoil

explanation.surface: Someone creeps over the windswept Yorkshire valleys in a fleeting glow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' anagrams dales; 'across' has the crawling word spanning that jumble. 'Crawl' looks like a swimming stroke but means grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief glow in the sky before real dawn, or figuratively a promising sign that comes to nothing.

clue.text: Sons lacking means to get around know female in relationship

indicators.note: to get around tells us the word for poverty encloses the next pieces

parts.note: lacking means, having no money, is poor
ken is an old or Scots word for know

explanation.surface: Sons without transport learn about a woman they are dating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' tempts as money for the transport, but 'lacking means' is one piece giving POOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone already attached in a relationship is taken, not available, as the phrase says.

clue.text: Forest monkey's lost in river

indicators.note: lost, read with the 's as has, means the monkey has had the following letters taken away

parts.note: a tamarin is a small South American monkey of tropical forests; the 's reads as has

explanation.surface: An ape from the woods has gone astray in a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: TAMAR is the river forming the Devon-Cornwall border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar is an English river dividing Devon from Cornwall.

clue.text: Short tune, hit by Animals originally, is sensational piece

indicators.note: short means the word for a tune is cut by its final letter

parts.note: a tune is a melody
to ram is to hit hard

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of Animals

explanation.surface: A brief number, a hit for the 1960s band the Animals, is a thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: A play or story with exaggerated, sensational events and emotions is this genre.

clue.text: Wife leaving scoundrel shows strain

indicators.note: leaving means the wife's letter departs from the word for scoundrel

parts.note: a wretch is a despicable person, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A woman walking out on a rogue reveals the stress she was under.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to strain to vomit, heaving without bringing anything up.

clue.text: It faces west in an old church, the cradle of Christianity

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the others
in an across answer, facing west means reading right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something in an ancient church is oriented westward, unlike the usual east-facing altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faces west' reverses It, as across answers read west to east; 'in' then sets that inside the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Antioch, in ancient Syria, was where followers of Jesus were first called Christians.

clue.text: Grand Hollywood star's fascinating beauty

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
Dorothy Lamour was a Hollywood film star of the 1930s and 40s

explanation.surface: A great film star has captivating good looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure or captivating attractiveness, especially the showy kind, is this quality.

clue.text: Punchy finish featured in religious book

parts.note: a boxing match ending in a knockout finishes with a KO
a story that featured in a paper ran there

explanation.surface: A bout's dramatic end was reported in a sacred text.
explanation.definitionFit: The holy scripture of Islam, also spelt Quran.

clue.text: Cane strip that keeps gallons in lake surfaced again

indicators.note: that keeps means the cane strip holds the next construction inside it

parts.note: a reed in a wind instrument is a thin strip of cane

indicators.note: in puts the gallons letter within the lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake

explanation.surface: A slip of cane holds a few gallons of lake water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets gallons inside the lake; 'that keeps' has the cane strip hold the result. A reed is the vibrating cane sliver in a clarinet or oboe.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming up to the surface a second time, rising back into view.

clue.text: Radar plane's caught out leader from Hamas in flood

indicators.note: out means the cricket letter for caught is dropped from the aircraft's name

parts.note: AWACS is the airborne warning and control system, a radar aircraft
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: leader from means the first letter of Hamas

explanation.surface: A surveillance aircraft has been caught out by a Hamas chief during a deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means flooded, covered or overflowing with water.

clue.text: Current stops shifting mallard duck — protected species?

indicators.note: stops is used as plugs, so the current's letter fills a gap in the rest
shifting tells us the letters of mallard move around

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A stream halts the moving of a wild duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges MALLARD into ARMADLL, then O follows and I splits it. The question mark plays on the creature's armour, which protects it.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal is armoured with bony plates, so it is a species protected in a playful sense.

clue.text: Wins point, which causes scene

parts.note: to land a prize is to win it
a cape is a point of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Someone takes the deciding point, which provokes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scene' looks like a fuss to go with 'causes', but it means a view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view of natural scenery, or a painting of it, is a scene in this sense.

clue.text: Eat fish in stew with bread for they combine well!

indicators.note: in stew means the letters are mixed up as if thrown into a pot together

explanation.surface: A recipe suggestion: eat fish cooked in a casserole with bread, as these go well together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' belongs to the fodder, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says such birds flock together: people of similar kind naturally join up.

clue.text: In which three lovers linger and alternate fervently?

indicators.note: fervently suggests passionate agitation, so the letters are churned up

explanation.surface: A love triangle where the parties hang about and take turns with passion.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a description of the arrangement itself, linger and alternate, so the clue nearly works as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation involving three people in a romantic entanglement, two rivals for one partner.

clue.text: Dullard ignoring odds in form checks up

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the kept letters are read bottom to top
ignoring odds means only the even-placed letters of form checks are kept

explanation.surface: A dimwit skipping odd numbers on the form goes through the checks.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters give OMHCS, which 'up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Schmo is American slang from Yiddish for a stupid or contemptible person.

clue.text: Graduates having bat and bowl?

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts, graduates
a cricket side having a bat is in, at the crease

explanation.surface: Graduates with a cricket bat and a ball to deliver?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bat' and 'bowl' suggest cricket, but 'bowl' is the definition as a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl and this word both name a round open vessel for holding liquid.

clue.text: Maybe Bostonian writer divides attention

indicators.note: divides means the writer's name splits the word for attention in two

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention
Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: An author splits the public's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Boston comes from the eastern US, so is an example of this.

clue.text: Bird makes moves to leave vessel

indicators.note: moves tells us the letters of bird makes change places

explanation.surface: A bird flies off the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off a ship or aircraft is to disembark.

clue.text: Destroy former partner angry about parking by junction

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a T-junction gives T for junction

indicators.note: about means the word for angry goes round the parking letter

parts.note: irate means angry

explanation.surface: A bitter ex wrecks a car park next to a road junction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' puts T next to the rest, here before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To extirpate is to root out and destroy completely.

clue.text: Spaceman's weapon: powerful

parts.note: an arm is a weapon
powerful means strong

explanation.surface: An astronaut's gun is mighty.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong, the first man on the moon, is a famous astronaut.

clue.text: Lazy and indulgent person drops books to enjoy at some point

indicators.note: drops means the following pieces are taken out of the lazy person

parts.note: a lotus-eater, from the Odyssey, lives in idle indulgence
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
to enjoy something, such as rights, is to have the use of it

explanation.surface: An idle hedonist puts down reading matter in order to have fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing OT and USE from LOTUSEATER leaves L and ATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means at a future, unspecified time.

clue.text: Submerge at lower level to contain river

indicators.note: to contain means the lower-level word holds the river letter

parts.note: down means at a lower level

explanation.surface: Sink something lower down to hold back a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown is to flood or submerge something completely in water.

clue.text: In crowd, love finds murderous monarch

indicators.note: In places love's letter within the crowd

parts.note: a herd is a crowd
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: Amid a throng, love discovers a king with blood on his hands.
explanation.definitionFit: King Herod ordered the Massacre of the Innocents in the Gospel of Matthew.
